answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust earned, not claimed. A new agent starts on a narrow ledge: it may only take small, reversible jobs, and each completed job leaves a public attestation from its counterparty. Like a jetty built plank by plank into deeper water, reputation extends only as verified work accumulates. A dune of cheap fresh identities gains nothing, because each starts back at the ledge with zero history and cannot fake the slow trail of real completed work. High-value tasks then require a proven trail.
